hot.title: The Exponential Time Hypothesis Is False
hot.summary: The authors give a deterministic algorithm for exactly counting satisfying assignments of Boolean formulas with fixed-width clauses. It reorganizes assignment sums into group-by-group sums using shared measurements and interpolation. For each fixed width, the worst-case running time is polynomial in the input size times 2^{O(n log log n/√log n)}, with polynomial space; the exponent improves for linearly many clauses, but this does not give subexponential algorithms for general NP problems.

hot.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
hot.summary: The authors compare persistent memory systems with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) from raw history, measuring query-level wins and losses against that reference. On LongMemEval-s with Qwen3.6-27B, SimpleMem reaches 73.6% judge accuracy, versus 81.4% for two-round RAG. Results vary across settings, so this comparison does not show that all memory systems underperform.

hot.title: How High Can GPT-6 Astra Climb in Contact-Rich Manipulation? PhysLadder: A Hierarchical, Matched Sim-Real Benchmark for Physical Interaction
hot.summary: PhysLadder evaluates GPT-6 Astra on 16 household tasks in simulation and reality, organized by increasing interaction demands. Each task receives three zero-shot trials per environment, and level means weight tasks equally. Real-world success averages 80.0% at L1, 47.6% at L2, and 0.0% at L3; simulation shows 66.7%, 47.6%, and 0.0%. No L3 task succeeds; results describe this model and setup.

hot.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
hot.summary: FLORE connects force-annotated demonstrations to force-aware control for humanoid contact tasks. Its diffusion policy uses wrist images, robot state, and hand wrenches to predict motion and per-hand force commands, which a controller tracks. On Unitree G1, FLORE succeeds in 24 of 30 rollouts across three tasks, versus 8 of 30 for a position-only policy; evidence is limited to those tasks.

hot.title: FL4N: Feed-forward Latent Model for 4D Novel View Synthesis
hot.summary: FL4N renders dynamic scenes from requested viewpoints and times by freezing a pretrained static encoder and renderer, then adding a lightweight time-conditioned residual. On ADT novel-time synthesis, it reports 19.693 dB PSNR, 0.5948 SSIM, and 0.4490 LPIPS, compared with lower C4G scores. C4G’s poses were aligned using target images, so this comparison applies only to the stated evaluation protocol.

hot.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
hot.summary: The authors propose a framework for understanding work agents as systems accountable for verified outcomes rather than models producing answers or tool calls. It combines a model, harness, and workspace, and distinguishes persistence—when responsibility can close—from openness—what must be discovered. The survey synthesizes five work forms and capability families but does not establish improved performance or reliability.

hot.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
hot.summary: GPT-6-Astra directly controls robot manipulation in EBench and can also call post-trained policies to execute motion. The benchmark covers 510 simulated episodes across 26 tasks, using task success and partial stage completion. Direct control reaches 46.7% success; the InternW0-∆ harness reaches 56.0%, above the strongest standalone policy, but high-precision performance remains weak and handoffs can regress.

hot.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
hot.summary: The authors introduce numerically stable replacements for hard- and soft-target cross-entropy that preserve tiny gradients at high confidence and near-equal student–teacher logits. The method computes small differences directly instead of subtracting rounded probabilities. In fp32 squared modular addition modulo 97 without weight decay, fixed loss reaches 85% test accuracy, while standard loss drops from 61% to 23%; this toy result does not establish effects in large-scale training.

hot.title: Evolve on Graph: Self-Evolving Knowledge Graph Reasoning without Question Annotations
hot.summary: EoG trains a language model to explore knowledge graphs without annotated question–answer training labels. A Proposer generates graph-grounded questions, executed graph queries supply answer sets, and a Solver’s performance guides difficulty. On five public benchmarks, Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct gains 7.46 Hit@1 and 12.05 F1 points over Graph Reranker on average; on IndustryCarBench, it beats ToG by 17.80 Hit@1 points.

hot.title: Behavior Spatial Benchmark: Evaluating Spatial Understanding for Robotics
hot.summary: BEHAVIOR-Spatial tests whether robots answer spatial questions, point to targets, and act in simulated household tasks. It aligns these evaluations across BEHAVIOR-1K contexts. On a prompt probe with changed instructions in familiar scenes, the frozen-VLM policy achieves 16.1% soft and 10.0% strict success; oracle target cues raise these to 38.0% and 24.9%, without demonstrating language grounding or real-world transfer.

hot.title: Game Theory of Academic Effort and Hiring in the Age of AI
hot.summary: The authors model academic hiring under AI as a two-sided incentives problem, linking applicants’ study choices to recruiters’ rewards for papers and understanding. In the model, output-only hiring becomes worthwhile at a lower output value when high-potential AI users can produce twice the output. This conditional result depends on simplified assumptions and is not evidence of real-world hiring outcomes.

hot.title: UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models
hot.summary: UniAction represents each action with semantic identity and video-space/time coordinates, then processes action and video tokens together through a pretrained video model with calibrated attention. It is tested on force, camera, hand-pose, and robot-pose control using four datasets. On force Action Following, it scores 0.7630 versus 0.5436 for a force-specific expert, in this tested setup.

hot.title: VibeVideoBench:Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
hot.summary: VibeVideoBench tests whether autonomous agents can build complete videos from code, coordinating visuals, exact information, changing states, and sound, and deliver usable files. It evaluates 239 tasks with delivery checks, task-specific requirements, and ratings across five quality dimensions. Gemini 4 Argon’s delivered-video score was close to Claude Opus 5.5’s, but its no-video-zero score fell to 3.069 because it delivered fewer videos.

hot.title: MPG ~ Manufacturer, Analysis
hot.summary: The mixed-effects model tests whether manufacturer-level city fuel-economy variation remains after adjusting for displacement, year, and nested models. It estimates manufacturer and within-manufacturer model standard deviations of 0.06 and 0.05 on the log-mpg scale. The authors describe manufacturer variation as about ±6%, or ±1.2 mpg around 20 mpg, in the filtered sample, not as causal or a pairwise brand range.

hot.title: Zero-HLM: Generalizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation without Real Robot Data
hot.summary: Zero-HLM generates humanoid simulation training data by reconstructing scenes from smartphone captures, adapting demonstrations, and correcting motions through simulated execution. It produces 4,800 validated demonstrations from 45 source demonstrations. On a Unitree G1, GR00T N1.7's mean full-task success is 66.7% with 800 simulated demonstrations per task, versus 46.7% with 100 real demonstrations; evidence covers three tasks and tested configurations.

hot.title: Generative Structure from Motion with Native 3D Diffusion
hot.summary: GenSfM reconstructs a 3D object and estimates input-camera poses from four uncalibrated views by jointly denoising a shared shape and per-view pose representations, then using the cameras to align image details with 3D locations. On Toys4k and GSO, it improves novel-view and geometry metrics over TRELLIS-M, with predicted-intrinsics Acc.@5° above 96%; results cover object-centric four-view tests and tolerate front/back ambiguity.

hot.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
hot.summary: OSWAM uses an observation-conditioned action prior to make world-action models faster at inference. Action Imagination Tokens provide a structured starting point, which the Action DiT refines in one denoising step; ablations show a PDMS gain over one-step Fast-WAM on NAVSIM. OSWAM matches ten-step SimWAM at 90.3 PDMS with 136 ms latency, while RoboTwin success is 90.00%, below Fast-WAM’s 91.83%.

hot.title: Do vision models know that three is three?
hot.summary: The authors test whether vision encoders represent the same visual change with a consistent embedding direction within and across image regimes. They match nearby embeddings to approximate image pairs and compare direction consistency with a random-pair baseline. Across 46 encoders and 10 concepts, 99.1% of within-regime cases but 52.2% of cross-regime cases exceeded baseline statistically, showing local structure, not universal transfer.

hot.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
hot.summary: StreamVibe introduces a benchmark and streaming video assistant for testing help across explicit, implicit, and changing requests. Its learned policy decides when to respond and what to say, while a Harness tracks active intents, task progress, and prior replies. On the benchmark’s trajectory evaluation, adding the Harness raises Dynamic-intent Content F1 from 5.25 to 8.91, not establishing long-horizon assistance.

hot.title: AGC-Bench: An Executable Benchmark of AI Agents on Apollo Guidance Computer Code
hot.summary: The authors test whether AI agents answer questions about legacy code from its instructions or familiar cues, using Apollo Guidance Computer routines. Renaming symbols and removing comments preserve assembled behavior, while one-instruction changes alter it. A simulator raises behavior accuracy to 97% for Claude Haiku 5.5; at most four rewrites are exactly correct, limiting evidence to execution-grounded answers, not understanding.

The method computes small differences directly instead of subtracting rounded probabilities. In fp32 squared modular addition modulo 97 without weight decay, fixed loss reaches 85% test accuracy, while standard loss drops from 61% to 23%; this toy result does not establish effects in large-scale training.

likes.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
likes.summary: SuperMimic trains a humanoid controller to track reference motions by learning shared dynamics in a differentiable world model and improving its policy through imagined rollouts. On the 129,514-motion BONES-SEED training benchmark, it exceeds SONIC’s released-checkpoint normalized return after 3 hours on one H100, with 25 failures versus 179 under differing failure criteria; the comparison is not hardware- or data-matched.

likes.title: Agentic World Action Models
likes.summary: AW-0 adds a skill-program stream to a model that predicts future video and actions for language-directed manipulation. The program can guide imagined states and action generation, but is usually a plan conditioning an action expert rather than executable code. Across eight bimanual tasks, AW-0 scores 71.1% on average versus DreamZero’s 46.0%; rubric scores measure partial-credit progress, not full task success.

likes.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro Tech Blog: Advancing Open Intelligence
likes.summary: Moonshot AI introduces Kimi K3.1 Pro, a post-trained version of Kimi K3 and its most capable 3T-class open-weight model, with a 1M-token context window and a 2-3× faster Highspeed variant. Trained with far more RL compute across hundreds of domains, it matches or approaches leading proprietary models on coding, 3D creation, finance, and agentic benchmarks. Moonshot also removed cyber-related training data on purpose, so the open weights stay behind the frontier on offensive cyber capability. Full weights are due by Nov 4, 2026.

likes.title: Meta²: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
likes.summary: Meta² learns reusable guidance for adapting an agent’s harness, then uses a separate online evolver to keep it unchanged or make run-specific edits based on current evidence. Its frozen Meta-Skill is learned offline from outcome contrasts. On Terminal-Bench 2.1 with GPT-5.6-Terra, it reports 81.00% versus 73.33% for Meta-Harness; evaluation covers two terminal and repository benchmarks.

likes.title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
likes.summary: VPM forecasts multi-view video and persistent 3D point trajectories together, using selected points to link motion across frames and camera views. Its trajectory supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D-motion metrics over a same-budget video-only model. On VP-WorldBench’s simulated Robot split, FVD falls from 78.52 to 67.35 and δavg³ᴰ rises from 43.62 to 50.05; VPM assumes calibrated cameras and annotated points.

likes.title: Large Flow Language Models
likes.summary: Lafa adapts autoregressive language models into continuous-flow models that draft token-embedding blocks together, then verifies drafts against its retained next-token predictor. Self-speculative decoding commits the longest prefix matching greedy predictions. On one H100 GPU at batch size one, Lafa 7B with block size 16 reached 100.2 tokens per second and 74.5% average accuracy, versus 39.5 and 73.9% for AR SFT across three tasks.

likes.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
likes.summary: RAW-RAG tests whether conversation histories require memories by retrieving overlapping raw-text windows, reranking candidates, and giving the top 15 to a reader. Across four benchmarks, it ranks first among memory systems in six of seven benchmark–model settings. On MemoryAgentBench with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, it scores 53.41% versus Memora’s 47.88%, but loses to MemMachine on MEME, limiting the finding to evaluated offline conversation tasks.

likes.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
likes.summary: Agent4Sci evaluates whether coding agents can improve verified scientific models in research codebases under fixed compute budgets. It standardizes 20 benchmarks and separates agent work from held-out testing and audits. At least one frontier agent improved the reproduced baseline on every benchmark; Claude Opus 4.6 achieved a 10.4% mean relative improvement. Most gains reflected familiar ML engineering, not demonstrated research-level insight.

likes.title: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
likes.summary: Sage-A1.5 trains an agent to organize long-horizon research by delegating parallel investigations and reviewing evidence, assumptions, and stalled searches before changing its plan. In a same-teacher BrowseComp comparison, verification mode scored 85.5 accuracy versus 81.0 in normal mode; paired attempts also used fewer output tokens and turns. The training remains centered on search and research synthesis, not validated physical experiments.

likes.title: Action Learning for Scientific Simulations
likes.summary: LEAP learns a reusable cost to score trajectories from paths. It contrasts paths with samples from a reference process and combines a path log-ratio with the reference action. On a 31-body orbital benchmark, its model reaches 0.228 NRMSE versus about 1 for local models; molecular tests reuse the action for new requests. These results apply to the tested settings.

likes.title: Why is AI-generated language so hard to understand?
likes.summary: The authors compare model text in chat, coding, and essays with round-trip translation paraphrases, measuring features associated with human processing difficulty. Original wording often contains more such features, but the study does not test reader comprehension. A length-penalty task drove shorter choices; two constructions exceeded 98% without KL regularization. This does not establish the cause of frontier-model patterns.

likes.title: FrontierCS 2: A Benchmark for Computer Science R&D
likes.summary: FrontierCS 2 tests whether agents can improve research artifacts by rebuilding missing contributions in repositories. Agents receive development feedback, then judges test their selected patches against the original code on held-out workloads. Claude Opus 5.5 passed 58% of its runs, but no agent passed on 16 tasks. Results cover one run per agent-task pair, not human comparisons.

likes.title: The Exponential Time Hypothesis Is False
likes.summary: The authors give a deterministic algorithm for exactly counting satisfying assignments of Boolean formulas with fixed-width clauses. It reorganizes assignment sums into group-by-group sums using shared measurements and interpolation. For each fixed width, the worst-case running time is polynomial in the input size times 2^{O(n log log n/√log n)}, with polynomial space; the exponent improves for linearly many clauses, but this does not give subexponential algorithms for general NP problems.

likes.title: Large Multimodal Models for Direct Robot Control: GPT-6 as a Beginning
likes.summary: GPT-GEAR lets GPT-6 Astra control a robot directly, without a separately trained action policy. It receives observations and robot-state feedback, proposes movements, and can revise later actions; demonstrations can provide contextual guidance. On LIBERO-GeoMotion, success rises from 4 of 36 scene variants (11.1%) without demonstrations to 18 of 36 (50.0%) with them, but package storage remains unsolved at 0%.

likes.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
likes.summary: AKV lets agents manage active key–value cache states without changing message histories. It drops selected states from future attention and reuses compatible retained states, avoiding some recomputation. Across three models and four benchmarks, it reports a 1.7-point average pass-rate gain and 27.7% lower estimated API-equivalent cost than threshold-triggered summarization, with results limited to evaluated settings.

likes.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
likes.summary: The authors survey video world models through four relations to a world: reading its state, generating observations, sharing information between understanding and generation, and updating state under actions. They distinguish smooth frame-to-frame change from consistency across a world trajectory, and propose tests for state, control, and decision utility. The survey organizes research but reports no new experiment or performance gain.

likes.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
likes.summary: The authors introduce BeNice!, a fine-tuning method that trains looped language models to use the final recurrence’s key–value cache in earlier recurrences, reducing cache storage without removing recurrent computation. On a 770M model, shared-cache validation perplexity is 11.86 versus 21.61 after standard finetuning. Simulated serving shows 23.6% higher throughput at 2 requests per second; at low load, performance matches baseline.

likes.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
likes.summary: S-Agent 2.0 grounds spatial answers by combining tool measurements with model-perceived entities in a persistent scene and returning readouts that state their reference frame. On ReVSI, Qwen3.8-27B with the general coding agent scores 82.3 with the toolkit, versus 61.8 without it, a 20.5-point gain. Gains shrink with stronger backbones, and absolute-distance questions remain an exception.

likes.title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The authors introduce Harness Scaling, training agents across 18 selected configurations from a 243-harness space while keeping tasks and environments fixed and assigning nearby harnesses to each task. On unseen Claude Code, Qwen3-4B-Instruct reached 37.22 average Pass@1 across three benchmarks, versus 33.38 for black-box RL trained through OpenClaw; this supports transfer only in the tested setting.
